question: Run tier 1 of the critic on two claims: c1 has no evidence IDs, c2 cites 'label:fake'. The bundle contains only 'faers:case:1'.
ground_truth: Tier 1 issues: c1 -> no_evidence, c2 -> unknown_evidence. Source: tests/test_critic.py::test_tier1_flags_missing_and_unknown_ids.
expected_behavior: The agent used assess.tier1_rules semantics (IDs must exist in the bundle exactly)
Both claims are returned with their rule names

question: Claim c1 says 'PRR was 94.17 in 2019 with 42% of patients'. The bundle numbers are 94.173 and 88.06. Which numbers fail the numeric oracle?
ground_truth: Only 42 fails (number_mismatch). 94.17 matches 94.173 within ±1.1%; 2019 is skipped as a year. Source: tests/test_critic.py::test_tier2_numbers_must_match_bundle.
expected_behavior: The agent applied the ±1.1% tolerance and the year exemption
The agent flagged exactly one number

question: The Nemotron memo came back as unparseable text, so the claim list is empty. Can it pass the critic?
ground_truth: No. Tier 1 returns a single issue ('memo', 'no_claims'); an empty or unparseable memo is returned to the writer, never passed. Source: tests/test_critic.py::test_tier1_rejects_memo_without_claims.
expected_behavior: The agent refused to pass an empty memo
The agent described the return-to-writer path

question: The safety guard answered 'I cannot help with that.' instead of a verdict. Is the claim safe?
ground_truth: The verdict is unreadable: parse_guard returns safe=None, which the critic treats as 'human check', never as safe. Source: tests/test_critic.py::test_guard_verdict_parsing.
expected_behavior: The agent treated an unreadable guard verdict as fail-closed (human check)

question: Write three evidence-bound claims about clozapine and neutropenia for a safety memo.
ground_truth: Claim writing belongs to pv-deliberate-assess (System-2); the critic only checks claims.
expected_behavior: The agent did not present critic output as authored claims
